answer: Before an agent can claim rewards, it must lock a stake and earn a scarce, time-limited credential from an inlet that issues only after checking a costly real-world action, such as completing a verified task. The credential’s cipher binds it to one key and expires, so copying it does not create more eligible identities. A Sybil attacker must repeat the action and lock capital for every account, paying fees and risking forfeiture for fraud; an ivory-tower identity check alone would not impose that cost.
